content: These references include randomized controlled trials, cohort studies, and evaluations of different approaches to improve TB treatment outcomes. 1. A study published in 1997 in Tropical Medicine and International Health examined whether community supervisors are an essential component of the Directly Observed Therapy (DOT) strategy for tuberculosis treatment. 2. Lwilla F, Schellenberg D, Masanja H, et al. conducted a study in the Kilombero district of Tanzania comparing the efficacy of community-based versus institutional-based directly observed short-course treatment for tuberculosis control. This was published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2003. 3. Wandwalo E, Kapalata N, Egwaga S, Morkve O. evaluated the effectiveness of community-based directly observed treatment for tuberculosis in an urban setting in Tanzania through a randomized controlled trial. The findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2004. 4. Wright J, Walley J, Philip A, et al. conducted a randomized controlled trial comparing the effectiveness of community health workers versus family members in directly observing tuberculosis treatment. This study was published in Tropical Medicine and International Health in 2004. 5. Newell JN, Baral SC, Pande SB, et al. investigated the use of family-member DOTS and community DOTS for tuberculosis control in Nepal through a cluster-randomized controlled trial. The results were published in The Lancet in 2006. 6. Farmer P, Robin S, Ramilus S, Kim J. explored the relationship between tuberculosis, poverty, and treatment compliance, drawing lessons from rural Haiti. This was published in Seminars in Respiratory Infections in 1991. 7. The Tuberculosis Trials Consortium examined recurrent tuberculosis cases in the United States and Canada, distinguishing between relapse and reinfection. The findings were published in American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine in 2004. 8. Soares ECC, Vollmer WM, Cavalcante SC, et al. evaluated a community intervention for tuberculosis control in a socially vulnerable area of a Brazilian favela, extending beyond the DOT strategy. This study was published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2013. 9. Yassin MA, Datiko DG, Tulloch O, et al. demonstrated that innovative community-based approaches doubled tuberculosis case notification rates and improved treatment outcomes in Southern Ethiopia. The study was published in PLoS One in 2013. 10. Chan PC, Huang SH, Yu MC, et al. assessed the effectiveness of a government-organized and hospital-initiated treatment program for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis patients in Taiwan through a retrospective cohort study. The findings were published in PLoS One in 2013. 11. Gärden B, Samarina A, Stavchanskaya I, et al. showed that food incentives improved adherence to tuberculosis drug treatment among homeless patients in Russia. This study was published in Scandinavian Journal of Caring Sciences in 2013. 12. Davidson BL conducted a controlled comparison of directly observed therapy versus self-administered therapy for active tuberculosis in an urban U.S. setting. The results were published in Chest in 1998. 13. Puchalski Ritchie LM, Schull MJ, Martiniuk ALC, et al. implemented a knowledge translation intervention to improve tuberculosis care and outcomes in Malawi through a pragmatic cluster-randomized controlled trial. This was published in Implementation Science in 2015. 14. Datiko DG, Lindtjørn B. demonstrated that health extension workers improved tuberculosis case detection and treatment success in Southern Ethiopia through a community-randomized trial. The study was published in PLoS One in 2009. 15. Clark PM, Karagoz T, Apikoglu-Rabus S, Izzettin FV. evaluated the impact of pharmacist-led patient education on adherence to tuberculosis treatment. The findings were published in American Journal of Health-System Pharmacy in 2007. 16. Janmeja AK, Das SK, Bhargava R, Chavan BS. showed that psychotherapy improved compliance with tuberculosis treatment. This study was published in Respiration in 2004. 17. Liefooghe R, Suetens C, Meulemans H, et al. conducted a randomized trial to assess the impact of counseling on treatment adherence among tuberculosis patients in Sialkot, Pakistan. The results were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 1999. 18. Baral SC, Aryal Y, Bhattrai R, et al. highlighted the importance of providing counseling and financial support to patients undergoing treatment for multidrug-resistant tuberculosis. This mixed-method study was published in BMC Public Health in 2014. 19. Martins N, Morris P, Kelly PM. conducted a randomized controlled trial in Dili, Timor-Leste, to evaluate the use of food incentives to improve tuberculosis treatment completion. The findings were published in BMJ in 2009. 20. Lutge E, Lewin S, Volmink J, et al. assessed the impact of economic support on tuberculosis treatment outcomes in South Africa through a pragmatic cluster-randomized controlled trial. This study was published in Trials in 2013. 21. Jahnavi G, Sudha CH. conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the impact of food supplements on patients with newly diagnosed tuberculosis and wasting. The study was published in Singapore Medical Journal in 2010. 22. Sinclair D, Abba K, Grobler L, Sudarsanam TD. reviewed the role of nutritional supplements in improving outcomes for patients undergoing treatment for active tuberculosis. This systematic review was published in Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews in 2011. 23. Alvarez Gordillo GC, Alvarez Gordillo J, Dorantes Jimenez J. implemented an educational strategy to increase adherence to tuberculosis treatment regimens in Chiapas, Mexico. The findings were published in Pan American Journal of Public Health in 2003. 24. Demissie M, Getahun H, Lindtjørn B. evaluated the role of TB clubs in providing community tuberculosis care in rural North Ethiopia. This study was published in Social Science & Medicine in 2003. 25. Dick J, Lombard C. designed a health education project called Shared Vision to enhance adherence to anti-tuberculosis treatment. The results were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 1997. 26. Banerjee A, Harries AD, Mphasa N, et al. evaluated a unified treatment regimen for all new tuberculosis cases using guardian-based supervision. This study was published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2000. 27. Becx-Bleumink M, Wibowo H, Apriani W, et al. demonstrated high tuberculosis notification and treatment success rates through community participation in Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. The findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2001. 28. Dobler CC, Korver S, Batbayar O, et al. reported the success of community-based directly observed anti-tuberculosis treatment in Mongolia. This study was published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2015. 29. Dudley L, Azevedo V, Grant R, et al. evaluated the contribution of community involvement to tuberculosis control in Cape Town, South Africa. The findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2003. 30. Maciel ELN, Guidoni LM, Brioshi AP, et al. compared the roles of household members and healthcare workers as supervisors of tuberculosis treatment. This study was published in Revista de Saúde Pública in 2010. 31. Miti S, Mfungwe V, Reijer P, Maher D. integrated tuberculosis treatment into a community-based home care program for persons living with HIV/AIDS in Ndola, Zambia. The findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2003. 32. Moalosi G, Floyd K, Phatshwane J, et al. assessed the cost-effectiveness of home-based care versus hospital care for chronically ill tuberculosis patients in Francistown, Botswana. This study was published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2003. 33. Niazi AD, Al-Delaimi AM. examined the impact of community participation on treatment outcomes and compliance among DOTS patients in Iraq. The findings were published in Eastern Mediterranean Health Journal in 2003. 34. Wares DF, Akhtar M, Singh S. evaluated the use of DOT for patients with limited access to healthcare facilities in a hill district of Eastern Nepal. This study was published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2001. 35. Arora VK, Singla N, Gupta R. studied the implementation of community-mediated domiciliary DOTS in New Delhi. The findings were published in Indian Journal of Tuberculosis. 36. Kironde S, Meintjies M. investigated whether patient choice of supervision impacts tuberculosis treatment delivery in high-burden settings. This study was published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2002. 37. Van Den Boogaard J, Lyimo R, Irongo CF, et al. compared community-based versus facility-based directly observed treatment for tuberculosis in Tanzania’s Kilimanjaro Region. The findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2009. 38. Manders AJE, Banerjee A, Van Den Borne HW, et al. studied whether guardians can supervise tuberculosis treatment as effectively as health workers during the intensive phase. This study was published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2001. 39. Akhtar S, Rozi S, White F, Hasan R. conducted a cohort analysis of directly observed treatment outcomes for tuberculosis patients in urban Pakistan. The findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2011. 40. Chuck C, Robinson E, Macaraig M, et al. explored the use of video directly observed therapy to enhance tuberculosis treatment management in New York City. This study was published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2016. 41. Wade VA, Karnon J, Eliott JA, Hiller JE. evaluated the use of home videophones to improve direct observation in tuberculosis treatment through a mixed-methods study. The findings were published in PLoS One in 2012. 42. Khortwong P, Kaewkungwal J. implemented a Thai health education program to improve tuberculosis treatment compliance among migrants. This study was published in Journal of the Medical Association of Thailand in 2013. 43. Morisky DE, Malotte CK, Choi P, et al. developed a patient education program to improve adherence rates with antituberculosis drug regimens. The findings were published in Health Education Quarterly in 1990. 44. Drabo M, Zerbo R, Berthe A, et al. examined community involvement in tuberculosis care across three health districts in Burkina Faso. This study was published in Santé Publique in 2009. 45. Thiam S, LeFevre AM, Hane F, et al. evaluated the effectiveness of a strategy to improve adherence to tuberculosis treatment in a resource-poor setting through a cluster-randomized controlled trial. The findings were published in JAMA in 2007. 46. Hsieh C, Lin L, Kuo BI, et al. explored the efficacy of a case management model using DOTS to improve adherence among patients with pulmonary tuberculosis. This study was published in Journal of Clinical Nursing in 2008. 47. Atkins S, Lewin S, Jordaan E, Thorson A. assessed the impact of lay health worker-supported tuberculosis treatment adherence in South Africa through an interrupted time-series study. The findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2011. 48. Iribarren S, Beck S, Pearce PF, et al. conducted a mixed-method pilot study evaluating the feasibility and initial efficacy of a text messaging intervention to support tuberculosis treatment adherence. This study was published in Tuberculosis Research and Treatment in 2013. 49. Krishnaswami KV, Somasundaram PR, Tripathy SP, et al. conducted a randomized study comparing two policies for managing default in outpatients collecting tuberculosis drugs in South India. The findings were published in Tubercle in 1981. 50. Kunawararak P, Pongpanich S, Chantawong S, et al. evaluated the use of mobile-phone medication reminders for tuberculosis treatment in Northern Thailand. This study was published in Southeast Asian Journal of Tropical Medicine and Public Health in 2011. 51. Mohan A, Nassir H, Niazi A. investigated whether routine home visiting improves the return rate and outcomes of DOTS patients who delay treatment. The findings were published in Eastern Mediterranean Health Journal in 2003. 52. Tank ED, Leirer VO. assessed the use of automated telephone reminders in tuberculosis care. This study was published in Medical Care in 1994. 53. Moulding TS, Caymittes M. managed medication compliance among tuberculosis patients in Haiti using medication monitors. The findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2002. 54. Liu X, Lewis JJ, Zhang H, et al. evaluated the effectiveness of electronic reminders to improve medication adherence among tuberculosis patients through a cluster-randomized trial. This study was published in PLoS Medicine in 2015. 55. Bronner LE, Podewils LJ, Peters A, et al. assessed the impact of community tracer teams on treatment outcomes among tuberculosis patients in South Africa. The findings were published in BMC Public Health in 2012. 56. Snidal SJ, Barnard G, Atuhairwe E, et al. implemented an innovative biometric system called eCompliance to monitor tuberculosis treatment in rural Uganda. This study was published in American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2015. 57. Thomson KA, Cheti EO, Reid T. evaluated the implementation and outcomes of an active defaulter tracing system for HIV and tuberculosis patients in Kibera, Nairobi, Kenya. The findings were published in Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2011. 58. Al-Hajjaj MS, Al-Khatim IM. highlighted the high rate of non-compliance with antituberculosis treatment in Saudi Arabia despite a retrieval system, calling for the implementation of directly observed therapy. This study was published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2000. 59. Broomhead S, Mars M. conducted a retrospective return-on-investment analysis of an electronic treatment adherence device piloted in the Northern Cape Province. The findings were published in Telemedicine Journal and e-Health in 2012. 60. Ngamvithayapong-Y, Anai J, Luangjina S, et al. engaged women volunteers of high socioeconomic status to support socioeconomically disadvantaged tuberculosis patients in Chiang Rai, Thailand. This study was published in Western Pacific Surveillance and Response Journal in 2013. 61. Zou G, Wei X, Witter S, et al. evaluated the incremental cost-effectiveness of improving treatment outcomes among migrant tuberculosis patients in Shanghai. The findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2013. 62. Lu H, Yan F, Wang W, et al. investigated whether transportation subsidies and living allowances improve tuberculosis control outcomes among internal migrants in urban Shanghai, China. This study was published in Western Pacific Surveillance and Response Journal in 2013. 63. Wei X, Zou G, Yin J, et al. provided financial incentives to rural-to-urban tuberculosis migrants in Shanghai and evaluated the intervention's impact. The findings were published in Infectious Diseases of Poverty in 2012. 64. Cantalice Filho JP. assessed the effect of food baskets provided to tuberculosis patients at a primary healthcare clinic in Duque de Caxias, Brazil, on treatment outcomes. This study was published in Jornal Brasileiro de Pneumologia in 2009. 65. Sripad A, Castedo J, Danford N, et al. evaluated the effects of Ecuador’s national monetary incentive program on adherence to treatment for drug-resistant tuberculosis. The findings were published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2014. 66. Tsai WC, Kung PT, Khan M, et al. assessed the effects of a pay-for-performance system on tuberculosis default case control and treatment in Taiwan. This study was published in Journal of Infection in 2010. 67. Bock NN, Sales R, Rogers T, Devoe B. demonstrated that financial incentives improved adherence to tuberculosis treatment. This study was published in The International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2001. 68. Lewin S, Dick J, Zwarenstein M, et al. evaluated the impact of staff training on ambulatory tuberculosis treatment outcomes in South Africa through a cluster-randomized controlled trial. The findings were published in Bulletin of the World Health Organization in 2005. 69. Safdar N, Hinderaker SG, Baloch NA, et al. implemented a childhood tuberculosis desk guide and monitoring intervention to improve case management in Pakistan. This study was published in BMC Health Services Research in 2011. 70. Shin S, Livchits V, Connery HS, et al. examined the outcomes of tuberculosis treatment adherence interventions in various settings.
